answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a shared task queue, then slash that bond when independent reviewers confirm deliberate fraud. One identity can still be copied into a hundred accounts, but every account must lock real value, so multiplying fake agents multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk. A ripple of coordinated votes from a raven or marble-themed swarm earns no extra weight unless those accounts survive review; the mechanism raises the cost of Sybils rather than pretending to make identities unique.
